sn35.105:1.1: “Bhikkhus, when what exists, by clinging to what, do pleasure and pain arise internally?”
sn35.105:2.1: “Venerable sir, our teachings are rooted in the Blessed One….”
sn35.105:3.1: “When there is the eye, bhikkhus, by clinging to the eye, pleasure and pain arise internally. When there is the ear …
sn35.105:3.2: the mind, by clinging to the mind, pleasure and pain arise internally.
sn35.105:3.4: is the eye permanent or impermanent?”
sn35.105:5.1: “Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?”
sn35.105:7.1: “But without clinging to what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, could pleasure and pain arise internally?”
sn35.105:19.1: But without clinging to what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change, could pleasure and pain arise internally?”
sn35.105:21.1: “Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple experiences revulsion towards the eye … the mind.
sn35.105:21.2: Experiencing revulsion, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion his mind is liberated. When it is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘It’s liberated.’
sn35.105:21.3: He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’”
